candidate.title: MAB-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina M.SssI methylase-assisted bisulfite sequencing (MAB-seq) component schematic for combined 5fC/5caC mapping in DNA: a conventional bisulfite control and an M.SssI-protected branch, each with a separate bisulfite-treatment/PCR-amplification block and DNA output. The caption and card identify MAB-seq as the target; Control is its illustrated comparator, not an additional named target method. CpG-specific interpretation follows the cited primary paper. The five icons are illustrative cytosine response classes. Unshown caMAB-seq, redBS-seq, reduced-representation, enrichment and analysis adaptations do not expand this scope; no complete adapter/library preparation or sequencing workflow is depicted.

states.label: DNA bearing unmodified and modified cytosines
features: Biological targets are 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) residues in DNA; the left highlighted DNA icon and caption identify these targets.
Initial symbols show C (green), 5mC (pink), 5hmC (blue), 5fC (cyan), and 5caC (orange). They illustrate five response classes, not an asserted contiguous genomic sequence.
The primary paper identifies genomic DNA as the substrate and CpG dinucleotides as the effective M.SssI protection context. No ends, adapters, attachment or compartments are depicted.

Results, [b00008], M.SssI pretreatment and CpG protection
evidence.quote: In MAB-seq, genomic DNA is first treated with the bacterial DNA CpG methyltransferase M.SssI, an enzyme that is originally isolated from Spiroplasma sp. strain MQ1 and is known to efficiently methylate cytosines within CpG dinucleotides 22. Bisulfite conversion of M. SssI-treated DNA may therefore only deaminate 5fC and 5caC; originally unmodified C within CpGs is protected as 5mC.

evidence.locator: Results, [b00008], non-CpG limitation
evidence.quote: Notably, MAB-seq is unable to distinguish 5fC/5caC from unmodified C within non-CpG context due to the poor activity of M. SssI towards C within non-CpG context.

evidence.locator: Online Methods, [b00051], raw MAB-seq readout and false-positive background
evidence.quote: In a MAB-seq experiment, 5fC and 5caC are read as T while unmodified C, 5mC and 5hmC are read as C. For a CpG site, if we name the number of T reads as NT and the number of C reads as NC, 5fC+5caC level (MAB-seq raw signal before background subtraction) can be calculated as NT/(NT+NC). Because conversion of unmodified C to 5mC by M.sssI cannot reach 100%, some T reads may come from incomplete methylation rather than real 5fC/5caC, leading to an overestimation of 5fC/5caC level.

states.label: Amplified control DNA encoding the standard bisulfite response
features: Upper response symbols are T, C, C, T, T for the input classes C, 5mC, 5hmC, 5fC, 5caC respectively.
The amplified DNA sequence carries the C/T response: T combines originally unmodified C with 5fC/5caC; C combines 5mC with 5hmC.
The generic rightmost DNA icon labels the product class; the figure shows no adapters, sequencing operation, or branch-pooling operation.

evidence.locator: Upper Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification block and TCCTT response symbols
Two rightward output arrows and common generic DNA label; no pooling junction is drawn
Results, [b00008], standard BS-seq conversion and resistance
evidence.quote: In standard BS-seq, C/5fC/5caC react with sodium bisulfite and are efficiently deaminated to uracil (C/5fC) or 5caU (5caC), both of which are sequenced as thymine (T), whereas 5mC and 5hmC are resistant to this chemical conversion and sequenced as C (Fig. 1a).

states.label: Amplified MAB-seq DNA encoding the combined 5fC/5caC response
features: Lower response symbols are C, C, C, T, T for the original input classes C, 5mC, 5hmC, 5fC, 5caC respectively.
Amplified DNA is the readout carrier. At effectively protected CpG sites its T fraction represents combined 5fC+5caC abundance; C combines originally unmodified C, 5mC and 5hmC.
5fC and 5caC are not distinguished from one another by this route. Incomplete M.SssI protection can cause false-positive T signals, and conversion efficiency affects the response.
The common DNA label does not establish mixing with the upper control product.

operations.label: Control
operations.description: Route the illustrated input DNA through the upper comparator without M.SssI methylation; the five cytosine modification classes are unchanged at this boundary. This records the depicted comparator path, not a chemical reaction or an asserted physical aliquoting procedure.
operations.information_effect: Retains the starting modification classes for the conventional bisulfite comparator.

operations.label: M.SssI
operations.description: Treat input DNA with M.SssI methylase. Unmodified C within CpG dinucleotides becomes 5mC, while the other four depicted cytosine classes remain as drawn. The enzyme is a catalyst, not a sequenced material or separate target workflow.
operations.mechanism: M.SssI is a CpG DNA methyltransferase; the introduced methyl group protects originally unmodified CpG C from the subsequent bisulfite C-to-T response.
operations.information_effect: Changes the chemical encoding so that originally unmodified CpG C joins the protected 5mC/5hmC response class; biological 5fC/5caC remain available to yield the T response.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Process upper control DNA by the two operations named in this combined block. Bisulfite changes the susceptible cytosines, and PCR produces DNA encoding their T response; the illustrated output changes from C/5mC/5hmC/5fC/5caC to T/C/C/T/T.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper reports bisulfite conversion of C and 5fC to uracil and of 5caC to 5caU, both read as T after amplification/sequencing; 5mC and 5hmC give C. The figure combines bisulfite treatment and PCR without depicting an intervening material boundary.
operations.information_effect: The DNA product preserves sequence-position association but collapses unmodified C, 5fC and 5caC into T, while 5mC and 5hmC collapse into C. It cannot identify the 5fC/5caC component of the T signal by itself.

Results, [b00008], standard BS-seq conversion and resistance
evidence.quote: In standard BS-seq, C/5fC/5caC react with sodium bisulfite and are efficiently deaminated to uracil (C/5fC) or 5caU (5caC), both of which are sequenced as thymine (T), whereas 5mC and 5hmC are resistant to this chemical conversion and sequenced as C (Fig. 1a).

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Process lower M.SssI-treated DNA in its own bisulfite/PCR instance. 5fC and 5caC yield the T response; the two illustrated 5mC symbols and 5hmC yield C, producing C/C/C/T/T in amplified DNA.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite converts the remaining susceptible 5fC and 5caC to the uracil/5caU products reported by the paper; subsequent amplification encodes T at these positions. M.SssI-introduced 5mC protects originally unmodified CpG C, while original 5mC and 5hmC also give C.
operations.information_effect: The DNA sequence carries a positive, combined 5fC/5caC signal as T at CpGs. It cannot resolve 5fC from 5caC or distinguish the original C/5mC/5hmC constituents of C. Incomplete methylation and inefficient target conversion limit quantitative interpretation; non-CpG T remains confounded by unmodified C.

The five icons are response classes rather than an asserted contiguous genomic sequence. The primary full text supports the CpG qualifier, combined target and efficiency limitations. No consequential diagram/paper conflict requires a correction: the drawing is schematic, and the candidate explicitly attributes these qualifications to the paper. The catalogue background sentence about methyltransferases and the generic uracil wording of the Neri abstract are not substituted for the depicted operation or the precise chemistry reported by Wu. All four reference leads and the sole target method have paper assessments; abstract-only support is explicitly bounded. No consequential unknown remains at this declared scope.
